result.title: Relational Bottleneck Models
result.summary: Achieving both interpretable and high-performance inference is a key challenge in deep learning. While Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) provide inherent interpretability, they are constrained by task-specific training and rely on isolated visual concepts that fail to capture higher-order visual semantic relationships. Conversely, Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate zero-shot capabilities through Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. However, standard CoT lacks a strict causal dependency between the generated rationale and the final output, compromising faithfulness. To bridge this gap, we propose Relational Bottleneck Models (RBMs), a novel training-free framework that transforms any off-the-shelf LVLMs into inherently interpretable models in a plug-and-play manner. RBMs consist of two stages: (i) Structured Rationale Generation (SRG), which explicitly models semantic interactions between visual concepts as subject-predicate-object triplets, and (ii) Rationale-Grounded Decoding (RGD), which enforces a strict causal dependency between the rationales and the final output. RGD aggregates rationale-conditional next-token distributions via an importance-weighted product-of-experts strategy, strictly excluding the image inputs from the decoding context. Extensive zero-shot evaluations across diverse benchmarks and LVLM backbones demonstrate that RBMs achieve superior interpretability while improving task performance over CBM baselines, entirely without task-specific fine-tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的 Relational Bottleneck Models，把现成 LVLM 转为可解释模型：先用主谓宾三元组显式刻画视觉概念间关系生成结构化理由，再用重要度加权的专家乘积解码，把理由当作答案的唯一因果依据。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从解码上下文中严格剔除图像输入、只让理由驱动答案」的做法，与 LVR 关心的答案是否真正使用中间推理状态、视觉旁路与理由忠实性直接可比，可供核查如何因果约束推理状态对输出的贡献；但状态为显式文本三元组而非 latent。
